analysis.title: "Over 80% Of Neoclouds Will Fold": Gartner Predicts A Bloodbath As CoreWeave Credit Prices In Default
key_insights: Gartner forecast on Oct 14, 2026 that by 2030 cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations.
CoreWeave closed down 15.5% at $65.78 (as much as -17% intraday). Its five-year CDS widened 135bps to a record 1,117bps, implying roughly 63% odds of default within five years.

Neocloud equities fell together: WULF -12.6%, CIFR -12.3%, IREN -12.2%, HUT -10.4%, NBIS -10.1%, APLD -9.4%. Goldman's Global NeoClouds basket (GSXGNEOC) fell 10.9%, its biggest loss this year. Nvidia fell 3.2%.

Gartner says AI data center owners need $8.5T of cumulative revenue through 2030 to cover announced capex, financing costs and a 12% return on invested capital. It forecasts no more than $3.6T of attributable AI revenue, a gap of about $4.9T.

Gartner sees nearly $1T of AI infrastructure spending in 2026 and another $6T over 2027-2030. It puts more than $3.5T of spending at risk of impairment by end-2030 and more than $4T of asset value at risk of write-downs through 2032. It does not expect the sector to clear the 12% hurdle before end-2032.

Gartner expects less than half of AI revenue to go to providers that own significant AI infrastructure. AI-optimized IaaS grows from $66B in 2027 to $174B in 2030, which Gartner calls too low for most AI compute providers to recover their investments.

Goldman's US equities desk closed with a note titled 'UGLY': the S&P had its first -1% SPX / -2% NDX move since late July. It cited focus on credit markets' view of AI financing and on neoclouds (-12%, a top-5 move in 5 years). Goldman's S&P ex-AI basket rose 61bps, one of the five biggest outperformance days of the year.

Goldman's Kaplan listed growing focus on neocloud credit and funding conditions among four factors that came to a head. CRWV questions were high, desk activity was underwhelming, investor anxiety was high, and info tech sell skew was the highest in over four weeks. Semis closed lower for a sixth straight session.
The selloff coincided with a hot core CPI (+0.33% vs +0.20% expected), which pushed December hike odds to roughly 87%. The 10-year yield is at 5.19%.

CoreWeave total debt was about $52B at end of June, up from about $15B a year earlier. Q2 interest expense was $640M vs $267M a year earlier, about a quarter of $2.58B revenue, against a $626M net loss.
D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria (Neutral, $100 PT) estimates CoreWeave borrows at about 9% and earns about 1% on its investments, and warned the equity value goes to zero if the AI spending boom turns.
CoreWeave's $8.5B DDTL 4, rated investment grade on a Meta offtake contract, pays a little over 2 points over SOFR. Its other delayed-draw term loans pay roughly 4 to 10 points.
CoreWeave 2032 unsecured notes ($1.25B) touched a 15% yield and closed at a record 14.5% on Tuesday. Unsecured bonds crossed 1,000bps G-spread for the first time on Oct 13.

Goldman cross-asset desk reported macro credit spreads widening the most in a single session in months: Oracle CDS +31bps, CoreWeave bonds down another 2 points, hyperscaler cash bonds 4-5bps wider, data center paper 7bps wider.
Morgan Stanley counts 20 project-finance-style HY data center bonds totaling $45.6B backing just over 4GW across eight tenants, with CoreWeave the tenant on seven. Many yield in the low-to-mid teens.

JPMorgan's Market Intelligence desk stayed Tactically Bullish and sees a possible opportunity to buy the dip in semis, while noting concern about a possible AI-related credit event behind the Treasury bid.

Goldman's rent math: short-term capacity deals fetch $40-50B+ per GW per year, long-term hosting $20-44B. Pricing the 2026-27 buildout at spot implies $1.8T of annual AI revenue vs end-demand in the low hundreds of billions. The author expects spot rates to converge toward term rates.
Goldman calculates $1.4T of 2028-2030 revenue is needed to justify the six largest US spenders' 2026-27 compute at a 15% ROIC and about $42B capex per GW, about $11.6B per GW per year.

The author argues Nvidia (reported $2B CoreWeave stake) can buy time with a bailout but cannot fix the economics, and expects more pain from equity-funding feedback, higher rates, and spot-to-term rate convergence.

tension_points.bull_case: Gartner frames the 80% figure as consolidation, which the sell-side spins as healthy: the strong absorb the weak, survivors buy GPUs at a discount, and the buildout carries on. JPMorgan sees a possible dip-buying opportunity in semis.
tension_points.bear_case: The author argues consolidation arrives through write-downs, distressed exchanges and restructuring calls, with CDS pricing better than coin-flip odds of a CoreWeave default by 2031 and Gartner's $3.5T impairment arriving early.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A funding or equity cushion that holds, such as CoreWeave CDS retracing from the record 1,117bps, or Nvidia support that restores capital market access.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have diversified cash flows and can wait for demand to catch up. Short-term capacity currently fetches $40-50B+ per GW per year.
tension_points.bear_case: Spot prices do not scale. Pricing the 2026-27 buildout at spot implies $1.8T of annual AI revenue vs end-demand in the low hundreds of billions, and Gartner sees only $3.6T of attributable revenue vs $8.5T needed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: End-demand for AI compute rising toward the revenue needed, or spot rates holding above term rates as new gigawatts come online.
